# Mac menu popover

> An animated macOS menu bar popover for React and shadcn, for Tauri and Electron apps.

- Docs and live demo: https://eased.dev/components/mac-menu-popover?ref=context7
- Source: [src/registry/eased/mac-menu-popover/](../../src/registry/eased/mac-menu-popover/)
- Installs: `components/eased/mac-menu-popover/mac-menu-popover.tsx`
- npm dependencies: `@base-ui/react`

## Install

```bash
npx shadcn add @eased/mac-menu-popover
```

Or by URL:

```bash
npx shadcn add https://eased.dev/r/mac-menu-popover.json
```

Import paths below assume the default `@/components` alias in `components.json`.

A macOS menu bar popover: a status item and a frosted panel that hangs from it on an arrow, built on Base UI Popover, the Eased floating layer and the shared `eased-mac` material.

## When to use

- A menu bar utility in a Tauri or Electron app: usage meters, timers, clipboard history, quick toggles.
- A web demo or landing page that shows a Mac app's tray panel and should look and move like the real thing.
- Anywhere a `Popover` should read as native macOS: system font, translucent material, an arrow pointing at its anchor.

## When not to use

- Ordinary web UI: use [Popover](https://eased.dev/components/popover?ref=context7), which follows Eased's web material and radius.
- A list of commands with no other content: a menu is the better pattern.
- Transient feedback such as volume or brightness changes: use [Mac HUD](https://eased.dev/components/mac-hud?ref=context7).

## Usage

```tsx example.tsx
import {
  MacMenuItem,
  MacMenuPopover,
  MacMenuPopoverClose,
  MacMenuPopoverContent,
  MacMenuSeparator,
  MacStatusItem,
} from "@/components/eased/mac-menu-popover/mac-menu-popover";

export function UsageMenu() {
  return (
    <MacMenuPopover>
      <MacStatusItem label="Tally: 62% of this session used">62%</MacStatusItem>
      <MacMenuPopoverContent>
        <p className="font-semibold">Tally</p>
        <p>62% of this session · resets in 1h 48m</p>
        <MacMenuSeparator />
        <MacMenuPopoverClose render={<MacMenuItem shortcut="⌘," />}>Settings…</MacMenuPopoverClose>
        <MacMenuPopoverClose render={<MacMenuItem shortcut="⌘Q" />}>Quit</MacMenuPopoverClose>
      </MacMenuPopoverContent>
    </MacMenuPopover>
  );
}
```

## Examples

### Kept inside a frame

In a mock-up, keep the panel inside the fake screen rather than the viewport.

```tsx
<MacMenuPopoverContent collisionBoundary={screenElement}>…</MacMenuPopoverContent>
```

### In a desktop tray window

On the desktop the native tray icon is the status item and a small borderless window is the panel, so render your content in `MacMenuPanel`: the same type, fills and padding, without the popover. `MacMenuItem` and `MacMenuSeparator` work inside it. In Tauri and Electron alike:

- The window draws real vibrancy and the panel uses `material="native"`, its default. A CSS blur can't see the desktop through a transparent window, so `"css"` there gives an unblurred tint; it is for web pages.
- Make the page transparent with `html, body { background: transparent; }`. shadcn's base layer paints `body` with `bg-background`, which covers the vibrancy.
- Call `useSystemAppearance()` once in the window. The vibrancy follows the system appearance and Eased's dark styles follow `.dark`; without the hook a dark Mac gets dark glass with black text.
- Size the window to the content (115px tall for the panel below) and hide it when it loses focus, as macOS does.

```tsx src/tray.tsx
import { exit } from "@tauri-apps/plugin-process";
import { useSystemAppearance } from "@/components/eased/lib/mac";
import { MacMenuItem, MacMenuPanel, MacMenuSeparator } from "@/components/eased/mac-menu-popover/mac-menu-popover";

export function TrayWindow() {
  useSystemAppearance();
  return (
    <MacMenuPanel>
      <p className="font-semibold">Tally</p>
      <p>62% of this session · resets in 1h 48m</p>
      <MacMenuSeparator />
      <MacMenuItem shortcut="⌘,">Settings…</MacMenuItem>
      {/* Electron: send an IPC message that calls app.quit() instead. */}
      <MacMenuItem shortcut="⌘Q" onClick={() => exit(0)}>Quit</MacMenuItem>
    </MacMenuPanel>
  );
}
```

`MacMenuPopover` itself is for menu bars drawn in the page: a web demo, a landing page, or an app window with its own title bar. If that window draws native vibrancy, pass `material="native"` to `MacMenuPopoverContent` too.

### In a Tauri app

Checked with Tauri 2.12, `tauri-plugin-positioner` 2.4 and `tauri-plugin-process` 2. Add the plugins with `tauri add positioner` and `tauri add process`, then turn on the tray features, which `tauri add` leaves off:

```toml src-tauri/Cargo.toml
tauri = { version = "2", features = ["tray-icon", "image-png"] }
tauri-plugin-positioner = { version = "2", features = ["tray-icon"] }
```

The window, hidden until the tray icon is clicked. `windowEffects` only works with `transparent: true`; `macOSPrivateApi` is not needed (a no-op since 2.12.1).

```json src-tauri/tauri.conf.json
{
  "app": {
    "windows": [
      {
        "label": "tray",
        "url": "/tray",
        "width": 320,
        "height": 115,
        "visible": false,
        "transparent": true,
        "decorations": false,
        "resizable": false,
        "alwaysOnTop": true,
        "skipTaskbar": true,
        "visibleOnAllWorkspaces": true,
        "windowEffects": { "effects": ["popover"], "state": "active", "radius": 12 }
      }
    ]
  }
}
```

A capability for the window. `process:default` is only for `exit`; a [Mac HUD](https://eased.dev/components/mac-hud?ref=context7) window gets its own.

```json src-tauri/capabilities/tray.json
{
  "identifier": "tray",
  "platforms": ["macOS"],
  "windows": ["tray"],
  "permissions": [
    "core:default",
    "core:window:allow-show",
    "core:window:allow-hide",
    "core:window:allow-set-position",
    "positioner:default",
    "process:default"
  ]
}
```

The tray icon opens the window under itself and hides it on blur. `show_menu_on_left_click(false)` replaces the deprecated `menu_on_left_click`; the icon is a black-on-transparent PNG that macOS tints as a template.

```rust src-tauri/src/lib.rs
use tauri::{
    image::Image,
    tray::{MouseButton, MouseButtonState, TrayIconBuilder, TrayIconEvent},
    Manager, WindowEvent,
};
use tauri_plugin_positioner::{Position, WindowExt};

#[cfg_attr(mobile, tauri::mobile_entry_point)]
pub fn run() {
    tauri::Builder::default()
        .plugin(tauri_plugin_positioner::init())
        .plugin(tauri_plugin_process::init())
        .setup(|app| {
            // A menu bar app: no Dock icon.
            #[cfg(target_os = "macos")]
            app.set_activation_policy(tauri::ActivationPolicy::Accessory);

            TrayIconBuilder::new()
                .icon(Image::from_bytes(include_bytes!("../icons/tray.png"))?)
                .icon_as_template(true)
                .show_menu_on_left_click(false)
                .on_tray_icon_event(|tray, event| {
                    tauri_plugin_positioner::on_tray_event(tray.app_handle(), &event);
                    if let TrayIconEvent::Click { button: MouseButton::Left, button_state: MouseButtonState::Up, .. } = event {
                        let Some(win) = tray.app_handle().get_webview_window("tray") else { return };
                        if win.is_visible().unwrap_or(false) {
                            let _ = win.hide();
                        } else {
                            let _ = win.move_window(Position::TrayBottomCenter);
                            let _ = win.show();
                            let _ = win.set_focus();
                        }
                    }
                })
                .build(app)?;
            Ok(())
        })
        // Hide the panel when it loses focus, as macOS does.
        .on_window_event(|window, event| {
            if window.label() == "tray" && matches!(event, WindowEvent::Focused(false)) {
                let _ = window.hide();
            }
        })
        .run(tauri::generate_context!())
        .expect("error while running tauri application");
}
```

### In an Electron app

The main process makes the tray icon and a hidden vibrancy window, and places the window under the icon on each click. `tray.getBounds()` can fall off every screen (an icon hidden behind the notch, or a second display), so the position is clamped to the nearest display.

```js electron/main.cjs
const path = require("node:path");
const { app, BrowserWindow, Tray, nativeImage, screen } = require("electron");

let tray, panel;

app.whenReady().then(() => {
  app.dock?.hide(); // A menu bar app: no Dock icon.

  panel = new BrowserWindow({
    width: 320,
    height: 115,
    show: false,
    frame: false,
    transparent: true,
    backgroundColor: "#00000000",
    resizable: false,
    skipTaskbar: true,
    alwaysOnTop: true,
    vibrancy: "popover",
    visualEffectState: "active",
  });
  panel.setVisibleOnAllWorkspaces(true, { visibleOnFullScreen: true });
  panel.on("blur", () => panel.hide());
  panel.loadFile(path.join(__dirname, "../dist/index.html"), { query: { view: "tray" } });

  const icon = nativeImage.createFromPath(path.join(__dirname, "trayTemplate.png"));
  icon.setTemplateImage(true);
  tray = new Tray(icon);
  tray.on("click", () => {
    if (panel.isVisible()) return panel.hide();
    const t = tray.getBounds();
    const { workArea } = screen.getDisplayMatching(t);
    const { width, height } = panel.getBounds();
    const x = Math.min(Math.max(t.x + t.width / 2 - width / 2, workArea.x + 8), workArea.x + workArea.width - width - 8);
    const y = Math.min(Math.max(t.y + t.height + 4, workArea.y), workArea.y + workArea.height - height);
    panel.setPosition(Math.round(x), Math.round(y));
    panel.show();
    panel.focus();
  });
});
```

macOS rounds the frameless window's corners (about 10pt) and draws its shadow; Electron can't round the vibrancy further.

## API reference

### MacMenuPopover

Base UI `Popover.Root`: `open`, `defaultOpen`, `onOpenChange`, `modal` (non-modal by default), `actionsRef`.

### MacStatusItem

Base UI `Popover.Trigger` props, plus:

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `label` | `string` | | Required accessible name, e.g. "Usage: 62% of this session used". |
| `className` | `string` | `""` | Appended to the item's classes. |

A 22px menu bar button. Children are its icon and optional short value.

### MacMenuPopoverContent

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `width` | `number` | `320` | Panel width, px; capped at the available width. |
| `arrow` | `boolean` | `true` | Draw the arrow. Without it the panel is a plain rounded rectangle. |
| `material` | `"css" \| "native"` | `"css"` | `native` drops the CSS blur and tint for a window that draws its own vibrancy. |
| `side` | `"bottom" \| "top"` | `"bottom"` | Flips on collision; the arrow moves to the facing edge. |
| `align` | `"start" \| "center" \| "end"` | `"center"` | |
| `sideOffset` | `number` | `6` | Gap from the status item to the arrow tip, px. |
| `alignOffset` | `number` | `0` | |
| `collisionPadding` | `number` | `8` | Space kept from the boundary, px. |
| `collisionBoundary` | `Element \| Element[] \| Rect \| "clipping-ancestors"` | viewport | The area the panel stays inside. |
| `initialFocus` | Base UI | see description | Where focus goes on open. Default: the first control when opened from the keyboard, the panel itself when clicked, so no row lights up. |
| `finalFocus` | Base UI | the status item | Where focus returns on close. |
| `container` | `HTMLElement \| null` | `document.body` | Portal target. |
| `zIndex` | `number` | `50` | |
| `className` | `string` | `""` | Appended to the content area (a flex column with 12px padding). |

The panel exposes `--pad` (12px) and `--radius-outer` (11px) for concentric children.

### MacMenuPanel

The panel's material, type, fills and 12px padding as a plain `div`, for a native tray window. `material` (`"native"`), `className`, `children`. It fills the window, so the window draws the corners.

### MacMenuItem

A `<button>` row. All button props, plus `icon` (a 16px icon on the content line) and `shortcut` (display text such as `"⌘D"`; wire the key yourself). Wrap it in `MacMenuPopoverClose` with `render` when the action should close the panel.

### MacMenuSeparator, MacMenuPopoverClose

A divider on the content lines (`className`), and Base UI `Popover.Close`.

### useSystemAppearance

From `@/components/eased/lib/mac`. Call it once in a Tauri or Electron window: it puts `.dark` on `<html>` while `prefers-color-scheme` is dark and follows changes, so the text matches the native vibrancy. It runs in an effect, so it is safe with server rendering. Eased otherwise follows `.dark` or `data-theme="dark"`, so leave it out of a web app with its own theme toggle.

## Keyboard

| Key | Action |
|---|---|
| `Enter` / `Space` on the status item | Opens or closes the panel. |
| `Tab` / `Shift+Tab` | Moves through the panel's controls; focus stays in the page. |
| `Esc` | Closes the panel and returns focus to the status item. |

## Accessibility

- The status item is a button named by `label`, with `aria-expanded` while open. Its visible text can be just a number; the label says what the number means.
- The panel is a Base UI popover (`role="dialog"`, non-modal). A keyboard open moves focus to its first control (a click focuses the panel itself); focus returns to the status item on close; Escape and an outside click dismiss it.
- Rows are real buttons. Hover and keyboard focus draw the same highlight, so focus is never invisible. The shortcut text is display only.
- The status item is 22px tall, as in the macOS menu bar; it sits in a dense row of targets, so it isn't enlarged to 44px.

## Motion

The panel grows from the arrow tip (Base UI's `--transform-origin`, which tracks the arrow) using the floating layer's transitions: it drops 6px toward the menu bar and scales from 0.95 on the `snappy` spring while fading in over 200ms, then leaves at half the distance and scale in 150ms. Open and close are CSS transitions, so a close during the open turns around mid-flight. The shadow layer copies the panel's motion state, so it moves in step. The status item presses and stays highlighted by colour only, never by scale. Reduced motion keeps a 100ms fade.

## Notes for AI

Pick this for anything that should look like a Mac menu bar extra. In a Tauri or Electron tray window render `MacMenuPanel` (native material by default) in a window with native vibrancy, a transparent `html, body`, and `useSystemAppearance()`. Compose `MacMenuPopover` › `MacStatusItem` + `MacMenuPopoverContent`, fill the content with your own layout, and use `MacMenuItem` / `MacMenuSeparator` for action rows. Always pass `label` to `MacStatusItem`.

Don't use `material="css"` in a desktop window: the blur can't see the desktop. Don't wrap the content in another card, border, shadow or blur: the panel draws its own material, hairline and shadow as one shape. Don't put a `filter`, `opacity` or `backdrop-filter` on an ancestor of the panel; it stops the blur from seeing the page. Don't scale the status item on press, and don't add animation to the panel: it already uses the shared floating motion.
